It has been alleged by the Prosecution that on 14.01.2021 at about 07:34 pm, at Iron Bridge, Delhi falling within the jurisdiction of Gandhi Nagar Traffic Circle, the accused was using his vehicle bearing number DL2CAU2370 without registration and was found carrying excess passenger and putting his private vehicle to commercial use and was also found using an alter seat in his vehicle State vs Dheeraj Gupta on 8 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/52925131/
1 and, therefore, was challaned for RC Violation under Section 39/192 of M.V. Act, 1988.

3. It is pertinent to mention here that the cognizance of the offence had already been taken by Virtual Traffic Court and a fine was proposed for the summary disposal of the case under Section 208, M.V. Act.

The accused exercised the option to contest the present challan on the web portal of Virtual Traffic Court, pursuant to which the present challan was transferred to this Court for adjudication as per law.

Proceedings before the Court:
4. Accused Dheeraj Gupta, entered his first appearance before this Court on 19.12.2024.
Notice under Section 251 Cr.P.C. was framed against him on 03.05.2025 to which he pleaded not guilty and claimed trial.

The accused pleaded that he had sold off his vehicle bearing no. DL-2CAU-2370 in the year 2016 to Regents PRANJALI by PRANJALI PRAKASH PRAKASH Date: 2026.01.08 TC No.

State vs. Dheeraj Gupta 14:20:14 -0300 Automobiles and he did not have the possession of the said vehicle at the time of the offence.
He further pleaded that he does not know how this vehicle came to be challaned in his name.
It was thus pleaded by him that he has not committed any offence in violation of the provisions of the M.V. Act and the present challan has been wrongly issued against him by the Traffic Police.
5. In order to prove its case, the Prosecution wished to examine one witness PW-1, Retired.
SI Narender Tyagi, S/o Late Sh. Kishori Lal.
PW-1, in his examination-in-chief deposed that on 14.01.2021, he was posted at Gandhi Nagar Circle as ZO.
On that day, a vehicle bearing no. DL-2CAU-2370 was driven by a person, namely, Ankit without registration.
The said driver was carrying 11 passengers in his vehicle exceeding the capacity and was found misusing his vehicle by putting it to commercial use.
He further deposed that he issued a challan and the same is exhibited as Ex. PW1/A & Ex. PW1/B.
He further deposed that he took the signature of driver Ankit at point B.

Ltd. in the year 2016.
8.
Thereafter, the matter was listed for Defence Evidence.

Accused examined himself as DW-1 and in his defence he placed on record his bank statement of September, 2016 reflecting the transactions made in his account by the insurance company when his vehicle was destroyed in an accident in State vs Dheeraj Gupta on 8 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/52925131/

He further deposed that the insurance company after returning the insured amount took the RC, duly signed Form 36 (sale letter form) and Bank NOC and the same is exhibited as Ex.DW1/A.
Appreciation of Evidence:
9. I have heard the arguments advanced by the Ld. Addl. PP for the State as well as the accused and have carefully perused the entire record and evidence placed before the Court.

10. In the present case, a violation of section 39 of M.V. Act has been alleged which reads as:-
Necessity of Registration:-
"No person shall drive any motor vehicle and no owner of a motor vehicle shall cause or permit the vehicle to be driven in any public place or in any other place unless the vehicle is registered in accordance with this Chapter and the certificate of registration of the vehicle has not been suspended or cancelled and the vehicle carries a registration mark displayed in the prescribed manner:

sentences.text:
In the present case, a violation of section 192 of M.V. Act has been alleged which reads as:-
Using vehicles without registration:-
(1) Whoever drives a motor vehicle or cause or allows a motor vehicle to be used contravention of the provisions of section 39 shall be punishable for the first offence with a fine which may extend to five thousand rupees but shall not be less than two thousand rupees for a second or subsequent offence with imprisonment which may extend to one year or with fine which may extend to ten thousand rupees but shall not be less than five thousand rupees or with both:
PROVIDED that the court may, for reasons to be recorded, impose a lesser punishment.

(2) Nothing in this section shall apply to the use of a motor vehicle in an emergency for the conveyance of persons suffering from sickness or injuries or for the transport of food or materials to relieve distress or of medical supplies for a like purpose:
PROVIDED that the person using the vehicle reports about the same to the Regional Transport Authority within seven days from the date of such use.

(3) The court to which an appeal lies from any conviction in respect of an offence of the nature specified in sub-section (1), may set aside or vary any order made by the court below,
notwithstanding that no appeal lies against the conviction in connection with which State vs Dheeraj Gupta on 8 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/52925131/
3 such order was made.
PRANJALI by PRANJALI PRAKASH PRAKASH

Date: 2026.01.08 14:20:33 -0300 3[Explanation:
Use of a motor vehicle in contravention of the provisions of section 56 shall be deemed to be a contravention of the provisions of section 39 and shall be punishable in the same manner as provided in sub-section (1).]

12. The primary objective of section 192 of Motor Vehicles Act is to ensure all vehicles on the road are legally registered, thereby allowing authorities to track ownership, ensure public safety, verify vehicle fitness, are enforced compliance with traffic laws, deterring the use of unregistered vehicles to penalties like fines and imprisonment, specially for repeat offenders, to maintain order and accountability in traffic management.
13. The cardinal principle of law in criminal cases is that the burden of proof lies upon the Prosecution to establish the guilt of the accused beyond reasonable doubt.
Thus, in order to prove the guilt of the accused and to warrant his conviction, the Prosecution is required to establish beyond reasonable doubt that the accused had indeed committed the violations.
14. Section 39 of the Motor Vehicles Act casts a prohibition on the driving of any vehicle by a person unless the same is registered.

15. In the present case, prosecution has placed on record the original challan and it is stated by the prosecution that a vehicle bearing no. DL-2CAU-2370 was driven by a person, namely, Ankit without registration and his signature was obtained on the PRANJALI by PRANJALI PRAKASH PRAKASH
Date: 2026.01.08 TC No. 7871/2022 State vs. Dheeraj Gupta 14:20:40 -0300 challan at point B.

sentences.text: However, upon perusal of the original challan, it has been seen that the said challan is blank and the ink has erased from it and the same has not been satisfactorily explained by the prosecution.
Nothing can be gauged from the original challan exhibited as Ex.PW1/A and Ex. PW1/B except the signatures of the driver Ankit and PW1.

Further, prosecution has brought nothing against the involvement of the accused in the violation in question and the testimony of PW1 is fixated on the point that the vehicle was being driven by one Ankit.
PW1 has also not explained as to why he did not inquire from the driver about the owner of the vehicle as section 192 of M.V. Act also imposes a liability upon the owner.
Nowhere in the testimony of PW1, named of the accused Dheeraj Gupta has come up.

Now coming to the testimony of DW1, it is the defence of the accused that his vehicle was destroyed in an accident in 2016 after which he sold his vehicle to Regent Automobile in September, 2016 and claimed his insurance amount and was not in possession or ownership of the vehicle at the time of the violation.
The accused has placed reliance upon the bank statement of September, 2016 when he got the insurance money from the insurance company.

A careful scrutiny of the bank statement and other documents placed on record by the accused show that the claim of the insurance was settled by the insurance company Regent Automobiles Pvt. Ltd. in September, 2016 and the insurance amount was also credited in the bank account of the accused in the same month.

State vs Dheeraj Gupta on 8 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/52925131/
4 16.
Considering the evidence on record, this court is of the opinion that the prosecution has not been able to prove its case PRANJALI by PRANJALI PRAKASH PRAKASH

Date: 2026.01.08 TC No.
7871/2022 State vs. Dheeraj Gupta 14:20:47 -0300 and has failed to fixate the liability of the accused in the commission of the offence in question.

sentences.text: On the other hand, the accused has successfully proved his defence by place on record material evidence that he was not in the possession of the vehicle at the time of the incident.
The defence of the accused that he had sold his vehicle to the insurance company in the year 2016 inspires the confidence of the court.

The challan in question is of the year 2021 and the prosecution has not been able to explain how the challan was issued in the name of the accused in 2021 when he was not in the possession of the offending vehicle at that time.
Therefore, the prosecution has failed to establish the guilt of the accused beyond reasonable doubt and the accused has been successful in raising a doubt in the story of the prosecution.

Conclusion:
17. In view of the reasons stated above, this Court is of the opinion that with respect to the offence under Section 192, M.V. Act, 1988, the ingredients of the alleged offence of RC violation do not stand satisfied before this Court and the guilt of the accused has not been established beyond reasonable doubt.
18.
In light of the discussion above, accused Dheeraj Gupta, S/o Jai Kumar Gupta in the present case stands acquitted for the offence under Section 192 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988.
